ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: search-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 14:44 UTC)
Alerting service: search
Alert time: 2026-07-29T14:44:00Z
Data available from 2026-07-29T13:00:00Z to 2026-07-29T16:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 7 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-07-29T16:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-07-29T13:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check the exact timeline and magnitude of the error rate spike.)
  Result: M-050: Change detected at 2026-07-29T14:40:00Z: mean 0.4 before, 22.82 after (235.8 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-050] search.error_rate_pct from 2026-07-29T13:00:00Z to 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.23 max=22.99 mean=10.36 last=22.77; mean=10.36. Change detected at 2026-07-29T14:40:00Z: mean 0.4 before, 22.82 after (235.8 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-07-29T13:20:00Z = 0.23 (lowest); 2026-07-29T14:40:00Z = 22.78 (first point after the change); 2026-07-29T15:05:00Z = 22.99 (peak); 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z = 22.77 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-07-29T16:00:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-07-29T13:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check CPU usage to see if there is resource exhaustion or traffic spike.)
  Result: M-047: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-047] search.cpu_pct from 2026-07-29T13:00:00Z to 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=31.14 max=42.86 mean=37.27 last=37.06; mean=37.27. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-07-29T13:10:00Z = 31.14 (lowest); 2026-07-29T15:35:00Z = 42.86 (peak); 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z = 37.06 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-07-29T14:50:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "deploy,config,error,warn", "service": "search", "start": "2026-07-29T14:30:00Z"} (asked because: Look for deploys, config changes, or warnings right before the alert.)
  Result: 6 matching log lines.
  [L-0244] 2026-07-29T14:33:38Z search INFO config heartbeat ok revision=195
  [L-0268] 2026-07-29T14:42:12Z search WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m

  [L-0293] 2026-07-29T14:48:57Z search WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
Step 4: metrics_query {"end": "2026-07-29T16:00:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-07-29T13:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if database connection pool exhaustion is causing the errors.)
  Result: M-048: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-048] search.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-07-29T13:00:00Z to 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=25.83 max=37.36 mean=30.81 last=30.11; mean=30.81. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-07-29T13:40:00Z = 37.36 (peak); 2026-07-29T14:30:00Z = 25.83 (lowest); 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z = 30.11 (last).
Step 5: metrics_query {"end": "2026-07-29T16:00:00Z", "metric": "cache_hit_ratio_pct", "service": "search", "start": "2026-07-29T13:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if a cache stampede or drop in cache hit ratio occurred.)
  Result: M-046: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-046] search.cache_hit_ratio_pct from 2026-07-29T13:00:00Z to 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z (36 points, 5-minute steps): min=90.5 max=94.43 mean=92.95 last=92.25; mean=92.95. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-07-29T13:00:00Z = 90.5 (lowest); 2026-07-29T15:20:00Z = 94.43 (peak); 2026-07-29T15:55:00Z = 92.25 (last).
Step 6: log_search {"end": "2026-07-29T14:45:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "deploy version start error exception timeout connect", "service": "search", "start": "2026-07-29T13:50:00Z"} (asked because: Search for deploy events, exceptions, or connection errors leading up to the incident.)
  Result: 8 matching log lines.
  [L-0119] 2026-07-29T13:50:11Z search INFO ranking model loaded version=v9.5.2 sha=b7229b0

  [L-0219] 2026-07-29T14:23:42Z search INFO ranking model loaded version=v9.4.1 sha=49c53e1
  [L-0268] 2026-07-29T14:42:12Z search WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0279] 2026-07-29T14:44:21Z search WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
Step 7: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "downstream timeout or high error rate in search service"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for high error rates and downstream dependencies to find mitigation steps.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-04-1 (similarity 0.64).
  [R-04-1] Downstream dependency timeout - Summary (similarity 0.64): A service is failing because something it relies on is slow or not answering. Calls to it run out of time, retries pile on extra load, and the failure spreads upstream to the callers of this service.
  [R-04-2] Downstream dependency timeout - Symptoms (similarity 0.64): The service looks unhealthy yet its own resources are fine. Responses are slow, then failures follow, and the delay seems to cluster right around the point where it waits for something it talks to. Protective cut-offs may start rejecting calls.
  [R-04-3] Downstream dependency timeout - How to confirm (similarity 0.62): Work out which neighbour the slow calls are going to, using the messages about calls that gave up. Then check how that neighbour is doing. If it is struggling while this service's own processor and memory look ordinary, the problem lives over there, not here.

Previous hypotheses:
- downstream_timeout: An abrupt spike in the error rate without any local resource exhaustion (CPU, DB pool) points toward a potential timeout or failure in a downstream dependency. (evidence: M-050, M-047, M-048, M-046)
- bad_deployment: The error rate spike occurs very abruptly at 14:40 UTC, which could still be related to a recent deployment or model version update that introduced unexpected failures. (evidence: M-050)
- misconfiguration: A subtle configuration or environment change could have been introduced around the time of the error increase causing validation or processing failures. (evidence: M-050)
